The **114th United States Congress** was the 2015-2016 session of the legislative branch of the U.S. federal government, composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives. The Republican Party maintained its majority in the House and won a majority in the Senate following the 2014 midterm elections. Of the 435 seats in the House, Republicans controlled 247 at the start of the session. According to *Daily Kos Elections*, 59 percent of House Democrats elected to the 114th Congress were women, minorities, or LGBT. There was also an increase in the number of Republican minorities and women elected on November 4, 2014. ### House of Representatives. Due to losing the majority in the U.S. Senate, Democrats lost a number of seats in Senate standing committees in the 114th Congress.

english_retrieval.title: Republicans win majority in US Senate, giving party full control of Congress | US midterm elections 2014 | The Guardian
english_retrieval.snippet: # Republicans win majority in US Senate, giving party full control of Congress. Mitch McConnell’s decisive victory in Kentucky sets ball rolling for Republicans in dismal election night for Democrats. Republicans swept to power in the US Senate after a rout for Democrats in midterm elections that were dominated by criticism of Barack Obama’s presidency and are likely to hobble his last two years in Washington. A stronger-than-expected Republican performance, including wins in states such as Colorado and Iowa that Obama carried in 2012, allows Republicans to take full control of Congress. Republicans captured Senate seats in West Virginia, Arkansas, South Dakota, Montana, Colorado and Iowa, and fended off Democrats in Kentucky, Georgia and Kansas, giving the party the 51 seats needed for a majority in the upper chamber of Congress. The presumptive new Senate majority leader, Mitch McConnell, pledged to work with Obama in the last two years of the president’s term after McConnell’s own decisive reelection victory in Kentucky began a steady rout for Democrats across the country.
